Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the model forecasts compared to true outcomes, taking into account the sentiment history.

## Example 1: Date=2024-08-13

History shows a downtick in the later days of the 30-day outcome:
- Days 16-30: [68.16, 67.00, 66.20, 66.50, 66.52, 64.92, 66.40, 65.45, 64.99, 63.21, 64.34, 63.70, 62.82, 63.39, 64.10]

But the model forecast was still mostly in the 70s, significantly higher than reality.

Looking at the divergence:
- Model was too high by ~1-4 points in early days
- The divergence widened in days 16-20 where model was still at 68-70 but reality dropped to 62-66

The model appears to be:
1. Too slow to recognize downward momentum
2. Has a bullish bias that gets invalidated by continued selling

Looking at sentiment:
- Sentiment became more positive (1.00) on day 16, then fluctuated
- But prices kept dropping despite positive sentiment in early forecast days

## Example 2: Date=2024-08-12

Similar pattern - model forecasts remain too high relative to reality. The divergence is most visible in days 16-20 where:
- Model: [68.16, 67.00, 66.20, 66.50, 66.52]
- Reality: [70.43, 68.16, 67.00, 66.50, 66.52] ... wait this doesn't match
